note: The 2026-10-22 pre-announcement (item 1, a mid-quarter statement made 22 days after quarter end) reset the bar below the stale consensus and the stock has sat flat for 12 sessions with shorts covering (item 4), so the formalised guide (item 0) is more likely to relieve than to disappoint.

A beat of the guide top is the base case (item 0) and this name sold three of its last four beat-and-raises (item 3); the raise that only passes the Q3 beat through leaves implied Q4 below the street's $472.6m (item 5) and Shopify's international deceleration (item 1) argues for a smaller beat, with a +6 put skew agreeing.

Cinemark +12.7% and AMC +23.3% attendance in exactly JJSF's Q4 weeks against a Frozen Beverages quarter that fell 8.3% a year ago (item 1) is a quantified counterparty read nobody has put in the $400.5m bar, offset by a +14.6% run in a month at 34.5x (item 4) and record diesel (item 2).

Home Depot's +2.2% US comp this morning against a ~flat LOW guide (item 0), corroborated by level Placer traffic (item 1), is the best evidence here, but LOW outran XHB by eight points on the post-midterm rally (item 2) and HD itself was sold -1.8% on the same beat (item 3), so the net is small on a 3.4% implied move.

Havertys' written comps collapsing from +12.3% to +2.3% in the same Southeast stores and the same Aug-Oct window (item 5), plus a Q3 guide that loses the acquisition's non-comp tailwind against a street at ~$0.59 (item 4) and a company that missed its own guide last quarter (item 1); the reset bar (item 15) and a +13.9-point put skew that already pays for downside keep it at this size.

The 5 November restatement of the FY26 and FY27 guides was made with Q3 closed and October in hand (item 0) and consensus now sits at the low end of the company's own Q3 range (item 4), against a 17% slide with no sourced cause and the absence of any new record-month PR (item 1), which is the honest counterweight.

guide_direction is 'cut' while impact_sum is positive on purpose: SQM has already fallen 35% since late August and 10% since Albemarle's print while ALB held, so the Q4 price cut is in the tape (item 3), and the analogue is ALB itself beating a lowered bar and rising 3.6% while guiding Q4 lower (item 1), with three consecutive bought prints behind it (item 4).

The payoff is asymmetric against a long: good growth prints earned 0.0%, -0.68% and +0.74% while the one gross-margin miss cost 29% (item 10), and the ADS has already rallied 15% in two sessions into the print (item 3) after an unexplained 47% slide that management never reassured on (item 12), which offsets the net-cash valuation and the near-secured GMV target (items 2 and 11).
